answer: Proof-of-stake reputation systems effectively mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to stake collateral to gain voting weight. An adversary attempting to create a sable layer of fake identities must bridge significant capital into the network, rendering the cost of identity fabrication prohibitively expensive. By tying influence to verifiable financial assets rather than a jade field of ephemeral nodes, the protocol ensures that economic rationality prevents any entity from cheaply manipulating consensus via volume.
